poisons.name: Acána
poisons.notes:
Black paste affects nervous system.
Extreme effect destroys nervous system and kills instantly.

poisons.name: Asgurash
poisons.notes:
Brownish red snake venom.
Moderate effect is upper body paralysis

poisons.name: Asp Venom
poisons.notes: When struck with an envenomed blade, the victim loses the use of the location for 3 days, during which time the limb is totally useless, alternately numb, aching or throbbing. If sandclaw leaves are crushed and packed into the wound within an hour of being hit, the herb neutralises the venom.

poisons.name: Bargolith
poisons.notes: Bargolist causes permanent loss of sight (Blinding) or permanent paralysis in one or more limbs, accompanied by excruciating, burning pain. Standard healing spells often cannot reverse the neural damage caused by Bargolith; it usually requires high-level magical restoration or rare specialised herbs (like Ankil) to repair the destroyed sensory pathways.

poisons.name: Black Clover
poisons.notes: Made from a paste from the pollen spores of the black clover plant, this poison was used by the Woses to coat their darts.

poisons.name: Blade Hemlock
poisons.notes:
This green paste may be applied to a blade with the following RR failure effects:
  • 01-25: abdominal cramps, nausea and vomiting, incapacitating them for 1-10 hours
  • 25+: convulsions and death in 6-10 rounds

poisons.name: Boglock
poisons.notes: Extracted from a desert cactus, if the poison reaches the bloodstream of a victim through food, drink or blade, it triggers muscle spasms of such a magnitude that the victim's heart is affected, killing them in 1-10 rounds

poisons.name: Brithagurth
poisons.notes: Black venom causing severe, rapid calcification and hardening of the skeletal tendons. Severe effects cause affected tendons freeze up entirely, making the limbs completely useless. The victim loses the physical ability to hold weapons, stand, or bend their joints, rendering them paralysed by their own rigid musculature.

poisons.name: Camadarch
poisons.notes: Camadarch is a liquid poison turning a victim's skin blue over the course of a day. After 24 hours, each external feature of the body must then make an RR or rot off in 1-10 hours. If mixed with alcohol, camadarch becomes an acidic contact poison that causes burns: 1-2 'E' heat criticals on the 1st round, 1-2 'C' criticals on the 3rd, and 1-2 'A' criticals on the 5th.

poisons.name: Carnegurth
poisons.notes:
The Primary Effect: It is classified as a Level 1 Circulatory Poison. If a character ingests it and fails their Resistance Roll (RR), the toxin enters the bloodstream.

The Consequences: The reddish juice causes widespread, massive blood clotting inside the victim's veins and arteries.

The Timeline: The target suffers excruciating internal blockages, culminating in total circulatory failure and death within 1 to 100 hours (determined by a rolling interval or GM discretion). Because it is a Level 1 poison, the Resistance Roll is easier to beat than high-tier poisons, but if the save is failed, finding an antidote (like Argsbargie) within the variable time window becomes an immediate priority.

poisons.name: Cathaana
poisons.notes:
White powder instantly causes mild euphoria (victim at -50 action for 1-10 rounds).
Extreme effect is that brain is destroyed after 1-10 minutes

poisons.name: Dynallca
poisons.notes:
Tan paste affects hearing and gives 1-10 hits.
Severe general effect destroys hearing.

poisons.name: Fangorth
poisons.notes:
This poison is harvested from a moss and stored in powder form, which may be blown into a victims face or deposited in food or drink.
Ingestion causes sleep for 1-4 hours, along with the typical respiratory effects.

poisons.name: Galenaana
poisons.notes:
A distinct green powder, that when ingested, the poison triggers a delayed or immediate systemic failure depending on the race of the victim:
  • Elves: Galenaana causes severe, fatal reactions in Elven biology. Failing the Resistance Roll results in extreme respiratory failure and death.
  • non-Elven targets (such as Men, Dwarves, or Hobbits), the maximum severity of the toxin is slightly mitigated but still catastrophic. A failed save drops the victim into a prolonged, deep coma lasting 1 to 100 weeks (1d100 weeks).

poisons.name: Gonhithui
poisons.notes: The paste causes dehydration over the next 24 hours for anyone who ingests it. In the most severe cases (failure by 101+), the victim dies from dysentery the following day. There is no known antidote for this toxin, but if the victim is kept warm and drinks nearly every waking moment, he may stave off its effects.

poisons.name: Grelnixar
poisons.notes:
Grelnixar hijacks the victim's nervous and circulatory systems, physically forcing them into a state of endless, fatal exhaustion.
If the victim fails their RR, the "Running Death" overrides the victim's willpower and motor controls. The character will bolt at top speed, sprint across the landscape, and cannot stop themselves until their body physically gives out and they die.

poisons.name: Hemlock
poisons.notes:
It may be deadly based on the RR failure:
  • 01-25: abdominal cramps, nausea and vomiting, incapacitating them for 1-10 hours
  • 25+ : convulsions and death in 6-10 rounds

poisons.name: Henuial
poisons.notes:
Yellow venom acts on victim's eyes.
Severe effects converts optic juices to honey

poisons.name: Hith-I-Girith
poisons.notes:
Mist/vapour from tree acts as depressant causing immediate and continuing sleep.
There are no other effects.

poisons.name: Jegga
poisons.notes: Brown paste gives 1-100 hits.

poisons.name: Jeggarukh
poisons.notes: Black powder gives 10-100 hits.

poisons.name: Jitsu
poisons.notes: Yellow venom gives 1-50 hits.

poisons.name: Jitsutyr
poisons.notes:
Tan paste.
Extreme effects destroys lungs and kills in 1-100 rounds

poisons.name: Juth
poisons.notes: Juth is only effective if administered by the edge or tip of a weapon. Orally ingested, it serves only to steal away the appetite of its intended victim. Anyone wounded with a juth-venomed blade finds his world eroding as he gradually goes insane, a hideous process that takes up to 1 week, First, the victim experiences 2-20 hits as the venom works its way into his system. An hour later, he suspects that friends are plotting to kill him. Yet another hour later, he becomes convinced of this and begins to hallucinate, usually about monsters or important figures, all of them out to “get” him. By the next day, the victim is violent if touched and paranoid about his possessions, fearing for thieves. The following morning finds he hears voices telling him to flee (50%) or kill everyone around him before they kill him first (50%). By the fourth day, the victim is a berserking, frothing, raving fool who either attacks or flees whenever contact is initiated by anyone else, From his perspective, the entire world is out to get him; he acts on this paranoia as if possessed until he either dies or is forcibly cured. Besides legendary cures, such as athelas or others, a brewed mixture of snowdragon and true tarnas, administered orally 3 times a day for 1 week is rumoured to be capable of reversing the insanity. A healer should be consulted in any case.

poisons.name: Kaktu
poisons.notes:
If consumed, kaktu acts as a powerful toxin, inducing numbness in all bodily extremities. If boiled and concentrated into liquid form, the flower becomes a more powerful poison that impairs a person's dexterity; this effect is permanent until an antidote is administered. The resulting palsy interferes with the victim's movement.
The poison affects 1-4 appendages, with Severe inflicting loss of 1-100 in temp Agility.

poisons.name: Kalmog's Spoor
poisons.notes: The poison reacts with blood, causing a burning sensation on the skin (2-20 hits over the next hour) that may become more severe, depending on where the paste touches the skin (i.e., more severe on the eyes and face). After a 24 hour incubation period, festering sores appear where the poison touched the skin. These sores hinder movement by -10 to -50, depending again on where they touched the victim.

poisons.name: Karfar
poisons.notes:
Reddish paste causes heart to malfunction.
All effects begin in 2-12 rounds

poisons.name: Kennesank
poisons.notes:
In it's native form this is a greenish gas, but may be dried to powder and blown into the face of a victim that burns the eyes, throat and lungs, delivering 3-30 hits.
Respiratory impairment continues to affect victims for a full 30 days, leaving them unable to exert themselves. Folklore maintains that sweet sorrel can remedy the damage.

poisons.name: Kly
poisons.notes: Anyone exposed to the toxin paste receives 3-300 hits over the next minute.

poisons.name: Klytun
poisons.notes:
Golden paste causes 1-10 day coma.
Effects begin after all general effects have begun

poisons.name: Lawrim
poisons.notes: When absorbed through the skin, the poison brings on a brief agony (all activities at -20) before causing paralysis (-01 to -100) which eventually wears off (1-100 hours).

poisons.name: Lhugruth
poisons.notes:
Grey/black blood affects exposed areas. 
Severe effects (dissolves inflicted area in 1-10 rounds)
Affects metal and organic material, not glass, sand and pottery

poisons.name: Limhereg
poisons.notes:
Contact with limhereg paste causes varying effects based on the RR failure
  • 01-50: skin peals away continually for 1-100 weeks, until the effects wane, the victim is at -25 and has ½ Presence
  • 51+: victim also bleeds through pores at a rate of 3 hits/round whenever he moves faster than half his base rate (a slow walk)

poisons.name: Lus
poisons.notes:
Lus paste is a contact poison with the following RR failure effects
  • 01-10: victim is temporarily blinded for 1-4 days
  • 11-20: blinded in either or both eyes
  • 21-50: slips into a coma and is blinded
  • 51+: dies within 1-12 rounds
The only known antidote is a mixture of atigax, klagul, megilloth and aldaka (which restores sight, removes the victim from a coma or reverses the effect of the poison if given within the first 12 rounds)

poisons.name: Madwort
poisons.notes:
The effects based on RR failure are
  • 1-25: induces madness for 11-20 rounds, causing him to tun about aimlessly, babble, attack friend and foe alike, etc.
  • 26-50: the poison inflicts 1-10 rounds of sensory disturbance, leaving the victim at -5O.
  • 51+: the resulting brain damage produce much more severe effects (10 to 20 points lost from the victim's potential Reasoning stat).

poisons.name: Malodorous Milkcap
poisons.notes:
This poison is a paralytic, with no other effects.
There is no antidote to this poison, but its effects wear off in 12 hours.

poisons.name: Metsästäjän Kukka
poisons.notes: This poison is extremely virulent and kills instantly.

poisons.name: Morhegen
poisons.notes:
Its victim's veins temporarily run with kalirion, a black liquid that serves as imperfect blood, sustaining life, but incapacitating.
Temporary mental stats (Em, In, Me, Pr, Re) fall by 50 but do not sink below I. The black-skinned victim returns to normal after 1-10 hours, but stats recuperate at rate of only 1/day. Some slave traders favour morhereg as a means of subduing their victims.

poisons.name: Muilfana
poisons.notes:
Orange tree sap affects mucous membranes.
Severe affects turns mucous to acid (blinds, or destroys windpipe and oesophagus)

poisons.name: Nen Calgalen
poisons.notes: Once it enters the bloodstream, it spreads a searing fire and disabling torment. The victim glows green and is often unable to move; some simply die, as their minds are torn apart by awful pain.

poisons.name: Nimnaur
poisons.notes:
Milky white juices affect organs.
Severe effects: liquefies one organ in 1-10 minutes, usually closest to entry point

poisons.name: Ondohithui
poisons.notes:
Blue/grey paste causes dehydration.
Extreme effect is fatal in 1-10 minutes

poisons.name: Ondokamba
poisons.notes:
Green venom acts on appendages.
Milder effects cause a mild temporary loss of dexterity in hands and/or feet.
Severe effects turns 1-4 appendages into stone

poisons.name: Poison Willow
poisons.notes:
Contact with this oily poison causes painful blisters within an hour that last for a week.
It is more an environmental hazard than an assassins tool.

poisons.name: Ruth-I-Iaur
poisons.notes:
Brownish cave-drake saliva.
Severe effects include erosion of nervous system in 1-20 rounds and victim left at -50 to -100 activity

poisons.name: Rúthin
poisons.notes:
Used as an ingested poison, an RR failure turns the contents of the victim's stomach into jagged shards of glass, causing death in 6-12 rounds. (There is no effect if the victim has
not eaten within the last 6 hours.)

poisons.name: Saewedhil
poisons.notes: A powder usually administered orally, it takes effect within seconds with deadly accuracy: Elves are killed instantly; all others are placed in a coma for 2-6 weeks.

poisons.name: Shagu-bitter
poisons.notes: This paste is an extremely toxic paralytic poison, which Orcish trackers sometimes place on their weapons.

poisons.name: Sharag
poisons.notes: As a poison, sharag may be administered through food or drink—not at sword-point. Taking effect within I minute, its victim feels his extremities go limp, one by one, until his lungs and finally his heart stops over the space of the next minute.

poisons.name: Sharduvaak
poisons.notes:
Brown liquid slows blood flow and victim needs double usual sleep until fully recovered.
These effects could last several weeks or months.

poisons.name: Sharkasar
poisons.notes: Brown paste gives 1-10 hits

poisons.name: Silmaana
poisons.notes:
Silver powder scars skin.
Gives 2-20 hits.

poisons.name: Skull Cap
poisons.notes: Skull cap is a deadly ingestive poison whose virulence operates upon its victim for a full 24 hours before abating.

poisons.name: Slird
poisons.notes:
Acts in 1-2 rounds.  
Moderate effects: victim loses feeling in 1-6 extremities (head, hands, genitals…) for 1-100 days

poisons.name: Slota
poisons.notes: Extreme effect is slow (1 day) paralysis and death (1-10 days)

poisons.name: Taynaga
poisons.notes: Brownish powder sterilises and gives 5-50 hits.

poisons.name: Traitor's Goblet
poisons.notes:
The flesh of a mushroom when eaten strikes its victim so quickly that no antidote may be administered in time.
If the flesh is dried the effect diminished to an attack level of 5.

poisons.name: Trusa
poisons.notes:
Mild effect is blindness in 1-2 eyes.
Moderate effect is complete blindness and coma.
Severe effect is death.

poisons.name: Ul-acaana
poisons.notes:
This is a 20th level nerve poison with the following effect:
  • Instant Paralysis: Upon failing the Resistance Roll, the poison immediately attacks the victim's central nervous system. The character is completely paralysed on the spot.
  • The Glassy Death: The poison works with horrifying speed, destroying the body's nerves. Mechanically, the target is struck into a coma or paralysed instantly, and they die within 1 to 10 minutes as their nervous system completely collapses as the poison literally hardens the victim's nerves into "glassy filaments."

poisons.name: Uraana
poisons.notes:
Creamy paste gives 3-30 hits.

Also known as Urána

poisons.name: Vuraana
poisons.notes: Pinkish paste delivers 1-100 hits.

poisons.name: Wek-baas
poisons.notes:
Acts in 1-100 rounds
Mild effect is deep sleep.
Moderate effect is degeneration of balance and hearing (-1 - -100 Agility and -50 to perception).
Severe effect is total paralysis.

poisons.name: White-Berried Yew
poisons.notes: Mature yew berries are extremely toxic, causing a quick and painless death in 1-10 rounds.

poisons.name: White Destroyer
poisons.notes:
If the target fails their RR the following effects occur:
  • 01-25: Slowness (-20) in limb closest to impact point
  • 26-50: 1-4 limbs become useless
  • 51+: Total paralysis

poisons.name: Witch's Pie
poisons.notes: The flesh of witch's pie tastes fine; however, 1 hour after consumption, the eater falls victim to its paralytic poison.

poisons.name: Wolfstooth
poisons.notes: It causes the heart to beat irregularly, incapacitating the victim for 10-20 rounds. Even if only moderately affected (RR failure of 26-50), the heart is damaged (-15 to 20 points from temporary Constitution). In some cases (RR failure of 51+), death results from heart failure.

poisons.name: Worlclivur
poisons.notes:
Worlcivur paste may be used as a contact or blade poison:
  • 01-30: blinded eye (-50) for 1-100 minutes
  • 31-60: induces random eye spasms for 1-100 days (on any roll of 01-25, the victim’s eyes flutter for 1-10 rounds, during which time he is at -75)
  • 61+: blinded in both eyes (-100) for 1-100 weeks

poisons.name: Zaganzar
poisons.notes:
Bluish extract.
Severe effect is to blind by reducing optic nerve to water.
Gives 1-10 hits.
